title: What Should a Medical Certificate Include?
description: What should a medical certificate include? Learn the details employers, schools and airlines check, and how a registered doctor issues one online.

blocks.text: A plain guide for people in South East Asia who need a doctor's note for work, study or travel

What should a medical certificate include, and how do you get one that your employer, school or airline will take seriously? This guide covers the details a certificate should show and when you need one.

On DrCertificate, an independent registered doctor reviews every request after a digital chat consultation and decides whether to issue a certificate. The service is for people in 10 South East Asian countries, from Singapore and Malaysia to the Philippines and Brunei.

The short answer on what a medical certificate should include

A medical certificate should show who it is for, the date of the consultation, the dates or fitness outcome it covers and its purpose, plus the doctor's name, qualification and registration details. On DrCertificate, an independent doctor decides after a chat consultation whether to issue one, and the receiving organisation decides whether to accept it.
Before you apply
What are the main facts about medical certificates?

items: A doctor makes the call Only the reviewing doctor decides whether a medical certificate is issued and what dates or fitness outcome it states.
Names must match The name and ID on a request must match. Mismatched details are one reason doctors decline about 2% of requests.
Duration has limits In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms. Fitness notes are generally valid for 30 days.
Acceptance is not automatic The employer, school or airline receiving the certificate decides whether it accepts an online medical note. Check first.

blocks.text: What is a medical certificate?

A medical certificate is a note from a doctor that records a medical opinion about you on a given date. It might say you are unfit for work or study for a set period, that you should work from home, that you are fit for a job, course, sport or flight, or that you are unfit to travel.
A medical certificate does not give a full diagnosis, a treatment plan or a prescription. It states the doctor's opinion, not your medical history.
Names get mixed up.
A sick leave certificate covers time off. A fitness certificate confirms you are well enough for an activity, and an unfit to fly note says the opposite for air travel.

On the DrCertificate form, a general medical certificate uses the Sick Leave option. Sports fitness, fit to fly and fit to work certificates use the Medical Fitness Certificate option. Unfit to fly requests use the Unfit to Travel option, and work from home notes have an option of their own.
When do you need a medical certificate?

items: You need a medical certificate when an organisation asks for proof from a doctor before it grants leave, accepts you or lets you travel. Work, university, school and air travel are the usual settings.

At work, HR or a line manager asks for one to approve paid sick leave or a work from home arrangement. In Singapore, the Ministry of Manpower says an employee must be certified unfit for work by a medical practitioner registered under the Medical Registration Act or Dental Registration Act to qualify for paid sick leave.
Universities and schools ask for one when you miss an exam, a deadline or classes. New employers, colleges and sports clubs may want a fitness certificate before you start.

Airlines are the other big one. Cebu Pacific, for example, asks for a valid medical certificate stating not fit to fly, with the doctor's signature, PRC number and official letterhead, when a passenger files a medical case request. The reason behind all of these requests is the same. Every one of these organisations wants a doctor, not the applicant, to confirm the health claim before it pays, excuses or changes something for you.
A note from a qualified doctor gives the organisation a record it can file and rely on if questions come up later.

blocks.text: A medical certificate at a glance

The number of days or the fitness outcome on a medical certificate is decided by the doctor case by case. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms, and fitness notes are generally valid for 30 days.
An in person visit suits you better if you need a physical examination, tests or care for worsening symptoms.

blocks.text: Who issues a medical certificate on DrCertificate?

A medical certificate on DrCertificate is issued by an independent certified doctor holding an MBBS, MD or MS qualification. Every doctor on the platform is registered with a medical council, and the doctor alone decides whether a certificate is issued.

DrCertificate is an online platform operated by Health Venture OU. The platform connects applicants with doctors through an online form and a digital chat, and DrCertificate does not diagnose, treat or prescribe.
That split matters.

The platform handles the form, payment and delivery, while the medical judgement sits with the doctor. Before you apply, check that the place you will submit the certificate accepts online medical notes. If your employer in Singapore needs a doctor registered under the Medical Registration Act, ask HR whether a note from a doctor registered with another medical council will be accepted.
How do you get a medical certificate online, step by step?
Getting a medical certificate through DrCertificate takes five steps, from choosing the right form option to receiving a PDF by email. There are no video or in person consultations at any point.

items: 1 Step 1: Choose the right option Open the online form and pick the option that matches your need: Sick Leave, Unfit to Travel, Work From Home or Medical Fitness Certificate. Fit to fly, sports fitness and fit to work requests use the Medical Fitness Certificate option.

2 Step 2: Fill in the form accurately Enter your name as shown on your ID, along with your symptoms or the activity you need clearance for. Wrong or inconsistent details are the usual reason requests are declined.
3 Step 3: Pay through Stripe Payment is taken through Stripe when you submit. Read the conditions first, because payments are non refundable.
4 Step 4: Chat with the doctor An independent doctor reviews your request in a digital chat, may ask follow-up questions, and then decides whether to issue a certificate.
5 Step 5: Receive your PDF If the doctor approves, the certificate arrives by email as a PDF, usually in about 30 minutes. Check every detail before you hand it in.

What should a medical certificate include?

A medical certificate should include your full name, the date of the consultation, the dates or fitness outcome it covers and the purpose, plus the doctor's name, qualification and registration details. Those are the details HR teams, school offices and airlines look for first.
Formats differ.

Cebu Pacific, for instance, wants a not fit to fly note with the doctor's signature, PRC number and official letterhead. Your employer or school may keep its own list. Ask for it before you apply, then run through the checklist once your certificate arrives.

items: Name matches your ID The spelling on the certificate matches the ID you will show.
Dates are right The start and end dates or validity period match what the organisation asked for.
Type fits the request The certificate type suits the purpose, for example sick leave, not fitness.
Doctor details are shown The doctor's name and qualification are on the certificate, along with any letterhead, signature or registration number the organisation requires.

blocks.text: Will your employer or school accept a medical certificate from an online doctor?

Your employer or school decides whether to accept a medical certificate, not the doctor and not DrCertificate. Acceptance rules differ between countries, companies and institutions, and an online note is not accepted everywhere.
Check before you pay.

A certificate is questioned most often when the wrong type was chosen, when details are missing or do not match the person's ID, or when the organisation only accepts doctors registered in its own country. That last point matters for paid sick leave in Singapore, where the Ministry of Manpower rule names doctors registered under the Medical Registration Act or Dental Registration Act.

If your certificate is questioned, ask the organisation in writing what it needs and why the note fell short. Share the doctor details shown on the certificate if they ask for them. If the organisation will not accept a note from any online doctor, a visit to a local clinic is the better route.

Keep in mind that an issued certificate cannot be corrected unless the error came from the medical team, and payments are non refundable. A short email to HR or the school office before you apply saves you from both problems.
When is an online medical certificate not the right choice?
An online medical certificate is not the right choice for urgent symptoms, legal matters, insurance or submission in India. DrCertificate is for suitable non emergency situations only.
Chest pain, trouble breathing, heavy bleeding or sudden weakness need in person or emergency care straight away.
Other limits apply too.

items: The doctor may decline Requests with mismatched names and ID, or inconsistent symptoms, can be declined, and the fee is not refunded.
Certificates are not for submission in India, not for legal purposes and must not be used for insurance.
Age 16 and over Applicants must be at least 16 years old.
Not every certificate is offered Recovery and caretaker certificates are not offered.

blocks.text: Medical certificate rules in Singapore, Malaysia and the rest of South East Asia

Medical certificate rules differ by country and by employer. A note that works for an office in Manila might not satisfy an HR team in Kuala Lumpur, and DrCertificate serves people in the 10 countries listed below.

Official rules sit with each country's labour ministry. In Singapore, that is the Ministry of Manpower. In Malaysia, check the Ministry of Human Resources, in the Philippines the Department of Labor and Employment, and in Thailand the Ministry of Labour.
Airline rules sit with the airline itself.
Before applying, confirm with your employer, school or airline that they accept an online medical note and what it must show.

blocks.text: What does a medical certificate cost and how long does it take?

A medical certificate on DrCertificate costs 25 SGD in Singapore, 399 pesos in the Philippines and 30 MYR in Malaysia. Prices in other served countries depend on the country. The fee covers the doctor's review of your request and, if approved, the certificate sent by email as a PDF.

A decision usually takes about 30 minutes. Timing depends on how quickly you answer the doctor's questions and on doctor hours, which for fitness cases run from 9 am to 9 pm IST Monday to Saturday and 10 am to 8 pm IST on Sunday.
Payments are non refundable, including when the doctor declines to issue a certificate. The only exception is a verified technical fault reported within 24 hours.

Frequently asked questions about medical certificates
Can a medical certificate be backdated?

Do not count on it. The doctor decides which dates a medical certificate covers, based on what you report in the chat consultation, and may decline dates the details do not support. Apply as soon as you feel unwell, and check whether your employer or school accepts notes covering earlier days.
How long can a medical certificate cover, and who decides?

The doctor decides the length case by case. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes go up to 7 days for generic symptoms, and fitness notes are generally valid for 30 days. If you need longer cover, see a doctor in person.
Do I have to talk to the doctor?

Yes, through a digital chat only. The doctor reviews your form and may ask follow-up questions in the chat before deciding. DrCertificate has no video calls or in person consultations. Answer promptly and accurately to avoid delays in getting a decision.
What happens if my request is declined?

You will not receive a certificate, and the payment is not refunded. Doctors decline about 2% of requests, usually when the name and ID do not match or the symptoms and details are inconsistent. If your situation needs care, see a local doctor in person.
Can I get a medical certificate for just one day?

Yes, if the doctor agrees it fits your symptoms. A sick leave certificate can cover a single day, and the doctor sets the dates after reviewing your request. Check your employer's policy first, because rules on when a note is needed for one day of leave differ.
Can I fix a mistake on my certificate after it is issued?

No, not unless the error came from the medical team. A medical certificate cannot be corrected once issued. Check your name, ID details and dates carefully on the form before you submit, because the payment is non refundable and a new request means a new fee.
